rationale: Published cohorts describing individuals with TAF4-related intellectual developmental disorder, autosomal dominant 73 (OMIM #620450) consistently demonstrate 100% penetrance of global developmental delay and intellectual disability (8/8 individuals, 100%, in the primary cohort cited in GeneReviews and Human Mutation). Associated speech and language delays are also consistently noted across disease databases and comparative reviews.

evidence.text: In comparative evaluations of TAF complex neurodevelopmental disorders, de novo putative loss-of-function variants in TAF4 are reported with developmental delay / intellectual disability present in 8 of 8 affected individuals (100%).

new_directions.question_text: Does detailed neuropsychological subtyping across expanded TAF4 cohorts confirm a statistically significant disparity between expressive language delay and receptive language or motor delay?
new_directions.rationale: While universal developmental delay and prominent speech delays are established in 100% of reported cases, formal quantitative profiling of expressive versus receptive language quotients has not been systematically published for larger patient cohorts.
